products.description_full:
My audiobook got rejected by ACX — how can I check every chapter against the ACX spec and fix it before I resubmit?
AudiobookSpecFix measures every chapter against the full ACX technical spec, fixes what a level/format pass can fix, then RE-MEASURES every output and hands you a fails-first report. Not a claim — a measurement. And it runs entirely on your computer: an unpublished manuscript is exactly the audio that should never be uploaded to a stranger's server.
WHAT IT CHECKS (every chapter, every run)
• Overall RMS — must land in −23 to −18 dB (full PCM decode, not a metadata guess)
• True peak — ≤ −3 dB
• Noise floor — the quietest 500 ms of the file must be ≤ −60 dB RMS
• Format — MP3 at 192 kbps constant bitrate (verified from the actual frame headers, so VBR can't hide)
• Sample rate 44.1 kHz · file length ≤ 120 minutes
• Head room tone 0.5–1 s · tail room tone 1–5 s
• One channel layout for the whole book (all mono or all stereo)
Spec as published in the ACX audio submission requirements, checked 2026-10-26.
WHAT IT FIXES
• Levels: gain / limiting into the RMS window, peaks held under the ceiling
• The odd stereo chapter in a mono book (or the reverse) — unified to the book's layout
• Room tone: missing head tone added, over-long tails trimmed — using the chapter's OWN room tone, carved from its longest quiet stretch
• Format: 128k VBR, 48 kHz, studio WAV — one final encode to 192 kbps CBR MP3 at 44.1 kHz
• Originals are never modified — fixed chapters + acx_report.md go to a separate folder
WHAT IT HONESTLY WON'T DO
• Pauses over 5 seconds are flagged with timestamps, never auto-cut — a dramatic pause might be the best beat in the chapter, and that's your call, not the tool's
• A noise floor recorded too hot (hiss printed into the take) cannot be fixed by levels: the chapter is reported UNFIXABLE with the maths shown, and no fake "fixed" file is produced. That one needs a re-record
• Passing these machine checks does not guarantee passing ACX's human QC — pronunciation, performance and extraneous sounds are not measured, and this page won't pretend otherwise
VERIFIED, NOT VIBES
Seeded acceptance test: 6 synthesised chapters with planted defects — RMS −30.3 dB; a −0.8 dBTP peak spike; a 48 kHz VBR encode carrying a 6.0 s interior pause; 0.00 s head tone with an 8.00 s tail; a stereo chapter in a mono book; a −49.8 dB noise floor designed to be unfixable. Result: 102 of 102 checks passed. Chapters 1–5 fixed and re-measured green on every check (RMS to −20.8 / −22.3 dB, peak spike to −3.9 dBTP, head tone 0.00 → 0.75 s, tail 8.00 → 2.50 s, VBR re-encoded to 192 kbps CBR with the 6 s pause flagged and kept — 25.2 s in, 25.2 s out). Chapter 6 reported UNFIXABLE, no output file. Zero new defects introduced; originals' SHA-256 hashes unchanged.
100% LOCAL & PRIVATE — no upload, no account, no subscription, no per-finished-hour metering. One purchase covers every book you ever submit.
Windows 10/11, nothing else to install. You get the fixed chapters + a plain-English before/after report (acx_report.md).

products.description_full:
How do I remove the duplicate messages that creep back into my MBOX archive every time I export, migrate or re-import my mail? And hiding in some archives is a nastier problem — messages silently split in half by an unescaped "From " line in the body, so pieces of your mail don't open anywhere.
MailMend cleans an .mbox archive (Thunderbird, Apple Mail, Google Takeout, any mbox export) on your own computer: duplicates removed, split messages rejoined, then the cleaned file is RE-PARSED to prove the result.
HOW DUPLICATES ARE CAUGHT — TWO WAYS
• By Message-ID, normalized — a copy whose ID differs only in letter case or spacing is still caught
• By content key (sender + subject + date + body) for messages that have no Message-ID — so a re-exported copy that only differs in its Received headers is caught too
WHAT IT REPAIRS
• Messages split by a fake envelope line in the body: the header-less fragment is rejoined to its parent message and the line is escaped — no content lost
WHAT IT NEVER DOES
• It never modifies your original file, never fabricates a Message-ID, and never guesses: kept messages are byte-preserved, attachments untouched
